collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — BELIEF, IDENTITY AND PERSONAL EXPRESSION (BLF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Religious, spiritual, atheist, agnostic, questioning and simply uninterested villagers living side by side; who people are, whom they love and how they present themselves. Privacy is respected, nobody has to explain or justify anything, and differences don't have to be the subject. Gods and spirits stay unconfirmed either way.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult)

collection.description: A young villager asks the oddest villager on Isola whether they mind being thought strange: laugh, or answer seriously.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) is, by general agreement, the oddest villager on Isola. (subject.He/she) wears a shell hat. (subject.He/she) talks to the lizards on (subject.his/her) roof by name. (subject.He/she) has a collection of interesting sticks, sorted by shape. Today a young villager, (friend), asks, "Don't you mind that people think you're strange?"

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) thinks about it. "I used to mind," (subject.he/she) says. "When I was your age. Then I noticed that people who think I'm strange still eat dinner with me, and still ask me about lizards. So I stopped minding." (friend) nods slowly. "I'm a bit strange too," (friend.he/she) confesses. "I know," says (subject). "I can tell. It's a good thing."

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: "Strange?" says (subject), delighted. "Me? Good! I'd hate to be boring." (subject.He/she) shows (friend) the stick collection. It takes an hour. (friend) is surprised to find it quite interesting. "Do you want to choose one?" asks (subject). (friend) chooses a stick shaped almost exactly like a fish. (friend.He/she) keeps it for years.
